cluster_summary: The cluster contains Java deserialization vulnerabilities where untrusted byte streams are passed to ObjectInputStream.readObject() (or Kryo) without any class allowlisting or type filtering, allowing arbitrary gadget-chain execution. Fix strategies vary: applying class allowlists via resolveClass or ObjectInputFilter, replacing native deserialization with manual parsing of primitive types, or removing the serializable classes entirely. One outlier is a JVM termination via System.exit, not a deserialization issue; another outlier has an incomplete fix that does not address the vulnerability.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-selected resource identifiers, object IDs, tenant IDs, or administrative action targets into sensitive read, write, mutation, deletion, workflow, or administrative operations on the selected resource. Report code paths where the authorization decision is not bound to both the current principal and the exact resource or tenant being affected. Confirm that the guard is enforced before the sensitive effect and remains bound to the same resource, principal, destination, or object that the effect uses. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 2 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should check ownership or tenant scope before the effect and carry that checked identity into the data access or mutation.

mechanism.missing_guard: the authorization decision is not bound to both the current principal and the exact resource or tenant being affected
mechanism.name: missing object-owner or tenant-scope authorization
mechanism.sink_shape: sensitive read, write, mutation, deletion, workflow, or administrative operations on the selected resource
mechanism.source_shape: attacker-selected resource identifiers, object IDs, tenant IDs, or administrative action targets
mechanism.typical_fix: check ownership or tenant scope before the effect and carry that checked identity into the data access or mutation

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Remove the Serializable interface from the vulnerable class, deprecate the class, or delete the entire deserialization code path so that no deserialization can occur.
sub_patterns.name: Elimination of serializable classes to prevent deserialization
sub_patterns.root_cause: The vulnerability exists because a class implements Serializable and is deserialized from untrusted sources without validation.
